claims.text: ATAM stands for Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method: it evaluates an architecture by walking its most important (prioritised) quality attribute scenarios through it and recording risks, i.e. where its decisions put those scenarios at risk.
claims.source_hint: ATAM method description (technical report introducing ATAM): purpose, scenario prioritisation, analysis of architectural approaches; glossary atam

claims.text: The full ATAM involves many stakeholders over several sessions; the reduced form used by Đơn Hàng is one session of the team and the product owner.
claims.source_hint: ATAM method description (phases and participants); docs/design/multi-shop-architecture-review.md @ stage-4 lines 11-12

claims.text: Review scope (lines 11-20): one session, whole team + product owner; evaluates ADR 0012's shape on stage-3 code; held end of Sprint 18 right after ADR 0012 was accepted, before building on it and before the data-layout ADR; does not re-decide ADR 0012, choose the layout or change load limits.

Drivers are CH-1 to CH-4 and YC-7; each is written as one or more scenarios. K1-K5 come from them with a measure; K6 is out of scope (no measure) and K7 an open question (measure awaits the product owner).
claims.source_hint: docs/design/multi-shop-architecture-review.md @ stage-4 lines 22-24, 39-40; docs/team/multi-shop-requirements.md @ stage-4 (Yêu cầu phi chức năng)

claims.text: K1 comes from CH-3: one shop's sale takes 10% of the day's orders; other shops keep normal-day targets: under 0.5% failed product reads, 99% of orders answered within 0.512 s.
Ranking rule (lines 28-30): product owner marks business importance, team marks difficulty; only scenarios High on both are analysed, which selects K1, K2, K4 (three of seven).

Lines 42-45: K3 and K5 not analysed because shop and configuration are data in ADR 0012's shape, kept as evidence for a trade-off point; K6 out of scope; K7 waits on an open question. K5 difficulty Medium; K7 difficulty High, measure 'Chờ product owner trả lời'.

The doc section after the excerpt: a weighted scoring matrix adds all criteria into one total per option; the review keeps scenarios separate so K1, failing badly with today's load limits, cannot hide behind K3 and K5; the matrix fits choosing among comparable options (the later email evaluation).
ADR 0012 serves every shop from one shared deployment, so isolation between shops is built inside the system, and leaves each shop's data layout to a later ADR.
For K1 the walk reaches the load limits in DonHang.Api/Program.cs (catalog-reads, orders), which count per process or per customer, never per shop, so one busy shop can use them up for every shop.
An evaluation's output should be a record per scenario, not one mark: a mark says neither which need is at risk nor which decision to revisit, and averages a badly failing scenario with passing ones.
Trade-offs table: no evaluation / reduced form / full method / scoring table, with cost, gain and failure mode; the full method costs more than a decision affecting one team needs.
A reduced review is worth its cost when the decision is expensive to reverse and nothing is built on it yet; it does not replace testing what is built later.

Choices: a library swap inside one module needs no session; picking among comparable email services fits a scoring table; a decision affecting three or four teams needs someone from each, possibly more than one session.
claims.source_hint: Outline items 5-6; ADR 0012 revisit conditions; multi-shop-requirements.md team-size driver

claims.text: Misconceptions: evaluation is not a score; a decision can be evaluated before it is built (Đơn Hàng's session ran right after ADR 0012 and found K1 failing with today's limits); not every raised scenario is analysed.
